blockAssessments.assessment: Paragraph 1 retains propagation of establishment of the electric field along the conductor, explicitly within this section's approximate description and close to the stated light speed of 300000 kilometers per second. It distinguishes that speed from much slower directed electron motion. Paragraph 2 introduces copper electron drift speed as the separate quantity to calculate. No universal exact conductor propagation speed or rapid individual electron transit is claimed.

Paragraph 3 retains formula (9-2), v=|I|/(|q0| n S), and a coherent strong-marked introductory sentence. Paragraph 4 explicitly uses current and electron-charge magnitudes and calls the result a speed, not a direction-bearing velocity. The title's conventional 'drift velocity' terminology does not override this explicit scalar calculation.

Paragraph 5 retains I=1 ampere, S=10^-6 square meters, and the electron's negative charge. Paragraph 6 correctly uses |q0|=1.6 times 10^-19 coulomb and explicitly scopes the one-free-electron-per-copper-atom model. Paragraph 7 retains shared valence electrons, free-electron number density n=8.5 times 10^28 per cubic meter, and the inherited exercise reference without creating a task. Paragraph 8 retains the exact substitution and v=7 times 10^-5 m/s as an approximation at the stated precision. Paragraph 9 preserves the fast-field/slow-drift distinction and says fast establishment of current does not require electrons first traveling the entire wire from the source. Only sentence continuity between paragraphs 5 and 6 needs revision.

Paragraph 10 identifies the water-filled pipe as an analogy, describes propagation of a pressure change at hundreds of meters per second, and contrasts the water's own flow at tens of centimeters per second. Paragraph 11 expressly separates propagation speed from material flow, then applies the analogy to field propagation versus electron drift. The scientific meaning is retained; the intended strong emphasis on the water-flow sentence is not correctly delimited.

conditionChecklist.condition: Field/signal-establishment propagation approximately near 300000 km/s in the stated section approximation is distinct from electron drift.
v=|I|/(|q0| n S) is a magnitude, not a signed vector velocity.
I=1 ampere, S=10^-6 m^2, electron charge magnitude 1.6 times 10^-19 C, and negative electron sign are retained.
One free electron per copper atom is a model; n=8.5 times 10^28 m^-3 is retained.
The original substitution and v=7 times 10^-5 m/s are retained at the stated approximate precision.
Fast establishment of current does not require individual electrons first traversing the entire wire.
Water-pipe pressure propagation at hundreds of m/s versus flow at tens of cm/s remains an explicitly qualified analogy.
